name: Booster, Master Cylinders & Reservoirs
description: Converts pedal force into hydraulic pressure. Factory: vacuum booster + tandem (dual-circuit) master cylinder on the driver-side firewall feeding the ABS/ESC modulator. Race: no booster; two independent master cylinders (front and rear) on the balance bar, each with its own remote reservoir.

components.name: Vacuum brake booster (factory)
components.description: Single-diaphragm vacuum booster bolted to the driver-side firewall; multiplies pedal force using manifold vacuum (supplemented on some engine combinations by a booster vacuum pump). Usually deleted on a race car because a cammy race engine makes little vacuum and the booster masks pedal feel.
components.location: Engine side of the driver-side firewall/cowl, x≈0.45–0.60, y≈0.80, z≈+0.42.

factory.name: GM power vacuum brake booster (Gen 6 Camaro)
factory.notes: Retained by 4 studs/nuts through the firewall; vacuum hose with check valve.

raceOptions.name: Booster delete (manual brakes with race dual-master pedal box)
raceOptions.notes: Block the firewall opening with an aluminum plate; requires smaller master bores (≈0.625–0.75 in) and higher pedal ratio.

hardware.item: Power vacuum brake booster nut (to pedal bracket/firewall studs)
hardware.notes: GM value "Power vacuum brake booster nut". Qty typical for this design.

installNotes: If retaining factory brakes: install booster with new gasket to firewall, then the master cylinder, before routing hard lines to the BPMV.
If deleting: seal the firewall hole with a riveted/bolted aluminum blanking plate with sealant.
inspection: Engine off, pump pedal to deplete vacuum; hold pedal and start engine – pedal should drop slightly (booster working).

sources.title: TightTorque – Chevrolet Camaro 6 (2016–2024) torque table, compiled from GM 2016–2018 Camaro service manual sections

modelRef.features: Black tandem-diaphragm shell, 4 firewall studs, vacuum check valve

components.name: Brake booster auxiliary vacuum pump (factory, engine-dependent)
components.description: GM service data for the Gen 6 lists a "power brake booster pump assembly" – an auxiliary vacuum source used where manifold vacuum alone is insufficient. Not needed once the booster is deleted.
components.location: Engine bay near the booster / front of dash (exact location varies by engine – verify on your donor).

factory.name: GM brake booster pump assembly
factory.notes: Torque values from GM SM table; mounting location not confirmed.

hardware.item: Power brake booster pump assembly bolt

installNotes: Only relevant if the factory boosted system is retained.

modelRef.features: Electric motor + pump head on rubber isolators

components.name: Tandem master cylinder with reservoir (factory)
components.description: Dual-circuit (primary/secondary) aluminum master cylinder bolted to the booster; two outlets feed the BPMV. Plastic reservoir with fluid level switch sits on top and also feeds the clutch master on manual cars.
components.location: Front of the booster, driver side engine bay, x≈0.30–0.42, y≈0.82, z≈+0.42.

factory.name: GM tandem master cylinder, Gen 6 Camaro

raceOptions.name: Replace with race dual-master pedal box

specs.Fluid level sensor: Reed switch in reservoir – triggers BRAKE warning

hardware.item: Brake pipe fitting at master cylinder outlet
hardware.spec: M12x1 / M10x1 ISO bubble-flare tube nut (verify)

installNotes: Torque nuts, then outlet tube nuts with a flare-nut wrench.
inspection: Check reservoir level and colour (dark = moisture) each event.

sources.title: TightTorque – Chevrolet Camaro 6 (2016–2024) torque table, compiled from GM 2016–2018 Camaro service manual sections

modelRef.features: Cast aluminium tandem MC, 2 outlets, translucent reservoir with level sensor

components.name: Front-circuit master cylinder (race)
components.description: Single-circuit master cylinder driven by the balance bar that feeds only the front calipers. Bore size sets pedal effort and travel: smaller bore = more pressure per pound of pedal force but more travel. With a 6-piston front caliper (≈ 25 cm² total piston area per side) typical bores are 0.70–0.75 in at ~5.5:1 pedal ratio.
components.location: Pedal box, driver footwell, pushrod forward, x≈0.70–0.82, y≈0.28, z≈+0.40.

raceOptions.name: Tilton 78-Series master cylinder (non-ABS)
raceOptions.notes: Bores 5/8–1 in, AN3 outlet, AN6 inlet, 3/8-24 pushrod, 1.1 in stroke. Tilton states NOT designed for ABS – use 79-Series when running Bosch ABS.

raceOptions.name: Tilton 79-Series (ABS-compatible) master cylinder
raceOptions.notes: Use with Bosch Motorsport M5/M7 ABS.

raceOptions.name: AP Racing CP7855 / CP2623 master cylinder

hardware.item: Master cylinder to pedal box mounting bolts
hardware.spec: 5/16-18 or 5/16-24 bolt (per pedal box), with washers
hardware.notes: Follow pedal box maker; do not crush the master flange.

hardware.torque: ≈ 110–130 in-lb (12–15 N·m) for -3 AN steel (typical); aluminum fittings lower
hardware.threadlocker: none (dry 37° flare; brake-fluid-safe lube on threads only)

installNotes: Bench bleed each master (outlet looped back to reservoir) before connecting lines.
Confirm pushrod free play so the compensating port opens when the pedal is released (residual pressure = dragging brakes).
If running ABS, use the ABS-compatible master model; do not run residual-pressure valves with ABS.
inspection: Check for fluid weeping at pushrod boot (seal failure).
Check reservoir level drop matches pad wear.

sources.title: Tilton Racing – 78-Series master cylinders (bores, AN3 outlet, AN6 inlet, 3/8-24 pushrod; not for ABS, use 79-Series)

images.title: Tilton 78-series master cylinder (Merlin) – 3.4 in body, 1.1 in stroke, AN3 out / AN6 in

modelRef.dimensions: Body ~86 mm (3.4 in), 1.1 in stroke, ~150 mm with pushrod/clevis
modelRef.features: Machined body, 2-bolt flange on the pedal-box bulkhead, AN6 inlet on top, AN3 outlet at the front

components.name: Rear-circuit master cylinder (race)
components.description: Independent master cylinder for the rear calipers. Usually one bore size larger than the front master (e.g. 0.75 front / 0.812–0.875 rear) so the balance bar sits near center for a typical ~65–70% front brake torque split on a front-engine car. Bias is then fine-tuned with the balance bar.
components.location: Pedal box, beside the front master, x≈0.70–0.82, y≈0.28, z≈+0.34.

hardware.item: Master cylinder to pedal box mounting bolts

installNotes: Bench bleed, install, connect -3 line to rear bulkhead / ABS.
Optional: inline adjustable proportioning valve in rear line only if bias range of the bar is insufficient.

sources.title: Tilton Racing – 78-Series master cylinders (bores, AN3 outlet, AN6 inlet, 3/8-24 pushrod; not for ABS, use 79-Series)

modelRef.features: Machined body, AN6 inlet, AN3 outlet

components.name: Remote brake fluid reservoirs
components.description: Separate reservoirs for front and rear masters (plus a third for the clutch master on manual cars). Mounted above the masters so fluid gravity-feeds; clear bodies let you read levels through a windshield-side inspection.
components.location: High on the driver-side firewall/footbox (cockpit side) or engine-bay side of the firewall, above master height: x≈0.66, y≈0.62, z≈+0.32…+0.44.

factory.name: Integrated plastic reservoir on tandem MC

raceOptions.name: Tilton remote reservoirs (with -4/-6 outlet)
raceOptions.notes: Pick capacity ≥ swept volume of a fully worn pad set.

fluids.name: Brake fluid
fluids.capacity: Fill to MAX with new pads

installNotes: Mount so reservoir outlets are higher than master inlets with no low loops in feed hoses.
inspection: Check level before every session; a sudden drop indicates a leak or boiled seal.

modelRef.features: Translucent white body, black screw cap, -4/-6 outlet, bracket

components.name: Reservoir-to-master feed hoses
components.description: Low-pressure hoses (typically -4/-6 AN or 5/16 in brake-fluid-rated hose) that gravity-feed each master from its reservoir.
components.location: Between reservoirs and master inlets, footwell/firewall.

raceOptions.name: Tilton / Wilwood reservoir hose kits
raceOptions.notes: Use EPDM-compatible hose rated for glycol brake fluid.

installNotes: Route continuously downhill to the masters; no loops above reservoir height.

modelRef.features: Hose with clamps reservoir -> MC inlet

components.name: Front & rear brake line pressure transducers
components.description: Data-logging pressure sensors (0–2000 psi / 0–140 bar) in each circuit. They give real brake bias (front ÷ total), driver braking traces and trigger the brake light via the PDM/ECU. Essential for setting a dual-master bias bar.
components.location: Teed into front and rear master outlets or a bulkhead/distribution block in the footwell.

factory.name: Factory pressure sensor is internal to the BPMV/EBCM (not usable for data without CAN)

raceOptions.name: Bosch Motorsport PSS-140 / AEM / Motec 0–2000 psi brake pressure sensor
raceOptions.notes: Typical 1/8-27 NPT or M10x1 port, 0.5–4.5 V ratiometric output.

hardware.spec: 1/8-27 NPT or M10x1 with sealing washer
hardware.torque: NPT: 1.5–2 turns past finger tight; M10x1 w/ washer ≈ 15–20 N·m
hardware.threadlocker: Brake-fluid-safe PTFE paste on NPT only

installNotes: Install in tees on master outlets before bleeding; calibrate zero with system bled and pedal released.
inspection: Check zero offset at start of each event.
